@ round, though groups of ravens may enter this area to forage. australian ravens will defend their territory by chasing, dive @ - @ bombing and occasionally striking the backs of birds of prey, foxes or even people. they generally mate for life, though occasionally one male has been found to be mated with two females in adjacent territories. if the female dies, the male australian raven maintains the territory and finds another mate, while\", \"title\": \"Australian raven\", \"source\": \"https://huggingface.co/datasets/Salesforce/wikitext/tree/b08601e04326c79dfdd32d625aee71d232d685c3/wikitext-103-raw-v1\", \"token_end\": 3604, \"license\": \"CC-BY-SA-3.0\", \"source_row\": 49964, \"token_start\": 3384, \"cosine_distance\": 0.31045806407928467}, {\"id\": \"passage-00016850\", \"text\": \"or restaurants, abattoirs, piggeries and farmyards. in one isolated study, they were observed feeding on nectar from eucalypt flowers. australian ravens sometimes forage in mixed @ -
